00022 /**

00026 {

00028     /**

00036     kHxFontSerif,

00038 
00039     /**

00041      * identified by the pFontName argument.  pFontName is the name of the
00042      * font file, with no path, and no extension.  The system font names
00043      * can be retrieved with the HxFontGetNames API.  kHxFontSystem should
00044      * be used to access the symbol, wingding, and Vera fonts.
00045      */
00046     kHxFontSystem,          
00047 
00048     /** 
00049      * @brief Use a font supplied by the application.  pFontName is the name
00050      * of the font file.  Unlike system fonts, the custom font name must

00053     kHxFontCustom

00057 /**
00058  * @brief Font weight definitions used by HxFontLoad.  These are bit flags:
00059  * bold italic = kHxFontBold | kHxFontItalic.
00060  *
00061  * When using the pFontname argument of HxFontLoad to load a system font or
00062  * custom font, the weight should be set to kHxFontPlain if the font name
00063  * uses the convention of defining the weight within the name (i.e.,
00064  * Verai.ttf, Verabd.ttf, and Verabi.ttf for italic, bold, and bold-italic
00065  * styles respectively).
00066  */
00067 typedef enum HxFontWeight_t
00068 {
00069     kHxFontPlain  = 0x00000000,      /**< default weight */
00070     kHxFontBold   = 0x00000001,
00071     kHxFontItalic = 0x00000002
00072 } HxFontWeight_t;

00075 /**

00079  * attributes.

00081 typedef enum HxFontAttributes_t
00082 {
00083     kHxFontAttrNone             = 0x00000000,  /**< none of these flags */
00084     kHxFontAttrNoKerning        = 0x00000001,  /**< don't use kerning */
00085     kHxFontAttrNoHinting        = 0x00000002,  /**< don't use hinting */
00086     kHxFontAttrMonochrome       = 0x00000004,  /**< don't use anti-aliasing */
00087 
00088     /**
00089      * @brief No char map is used: glyph indices are specified directly in
00090      * the string.
00091      */
00092     kHxFontAttrNoCharMap        = 0x00000008,
00093 
00094     /**
00095      * @brief Use fractional numbers for the font size with 26.6 fixed point
00096      * numbers.  Fractional sizes are not available for the default font.
00097      */
00098     kHxFontAttrFractionalSizes  = 0x00000010,
00099 
00100     /**
00101      * @brief If this attribute is set, then the sizes passed to HxFontLoad
00102      * is interpreted as points rather than pixels.

00140 /**
00141  * @brief               Load a font
00142  *
00143  * HxFontLoad returns the HxFont_t structure specified by the arguments.
00144  * HxFont_t is an opaque structure that is used by the font and string
00145  * measurement API.
00146  *
00147  * By default, the size is in screen pixels.  If the kHxFontAttrPoints 
00148  * attribute is used, size is in points.
00149  *
00150  * pFontName should be set to NULL for system fonts. 
00151  *
00152  * If the requested font is not found, the default plain font is returned.
00153  * An exception to this rule is a request for symbol or wingding fonts: the
00154  * plain symbol or wingding font is always returned, even when the weight
00155  * is set to bold and/or italic.                                                              
00156  *
00157  * After using the font, unload the font using HxFontUnload.
00158  *
00159  * @param family        IN:     See HxFontFamily_t definition
00160  * @param size          IN:     Size of the font
00161  * @param weight        IN:     See HxFontWeight_t definition
00162  * @param attributes    IN:     See HxFontAttributes_t definition
00163  * @param pFontName     IN:     The name of an application font, or NULL
00164  * @param hFont         OUT:    Returns HxFont_t if successful
00165  *                              
00166  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00167  *                              Returns HX_MISSING_FILE if the requested 
00168  *                              font and the default font are not found.
00169  *
00170  **/
00171 HxResult HxFontLoad(HxFontFamily_t family, int32_t size, HxFontWeight_t weight,
00172                     HxFontAttributes_t attributes, const char* pFontName,
00173                     HxFont_t** hFont);

00175 /**

00177  *
00178  * HxFontUnload unloads a font that had been loaded through an earlier call
00179  * to HxFontLoad.

00181  * In general, applications should unload fonts that are rarely used in order
00182  * keep a smaller memory footprint.  Internally, a reference count is
00183  * maintained, so that the font is actually unloaded only after the last
00184  * user within the application of that particular font calls HxFontUnload.
00185  *
00186  * @param pFont         IN:     Pointer to font
00187  *
00188  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00189  *
00190  **/
00191 HxResult HxFontUnload(HxFont_t* pFont);

00194 /**
00195  * @brief               Make a copy of a font
00196  *
00197  * HxFontCopy returns a copy of the source HxFont_t object.
00198  *
00199  * Call this function when the application needs to keep a reference for a
00200  * font independent from its use by widgets.  By calling this function, the
00201  * reference count for the font is incremented, preventing the untimely
00202  * deallocation of the underlying font interface when all widgets associated
00203  * with the font are deleted. 
00204  *
00205  * After using the font copy, release the font using HxFontUnload.
00206  *
00207  * HX_NULL_POINTER is returned if pSrcFont is NULL.
00208  *
00209  * @param hDestFont     OUT:    Returns HxFont_t if successful
00210  * @param pSrcFont      IN:     Pointer to source font
00211  *
00212  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK if successful.
00213  *
00214  **/
00215 HxResult HxFontCopy(HxFont_t** hDestFont, HxFont_t* pSrcFont);

00404 /**
00405  * @brief               Return the string extents
00406  *
00407  * HxFontGetStringExtents returns the logical and real extents of the specified
00408  * UTF-8 string.  The logical rectangle describes the typographic extents and
00409  * should be used to lay out text. The ink rectangle describes the smallest
00410  * rectangle containing all pixels that are touched when drawing the string. If
00411  * you only need one of the rectangles, pass NULL for the other one.
00412  *
00413  * The ink rectangle is guaranteed to be a valid rectangle with positive width
00414  * and height, while the logical rectangle may have negative width indicating
00415  * right-to-left layout.
00416  *
00417  * The rectangle offsets are reported relative to the baseline and refer to
00418  * the text being drawn using left alignment.  Note that this is a different
00419  * origin than the default top-left origin used when drawing text.
00420  *
00421  * The string measurement stops when a newline character is found.  The count
00422  * includes the newline character byte.
00423  *
00424  * Note that this function can be used to measure the drawn dimensions of a
00425  * single glyph (for example, the lower case 'x'), by passing the string "x",
00426  * setting pRectLogical to NULL, and setting pRectInk to a valid pointer.
00427  *
00428  * If pFont is set to NULL, the default system font is used.
00429  *
00430  * @param pFont         IN:     Pointer to font, or NULL
00431  * @param pString       IN:     String to be measured   
00432  * @param pRectLogical  OUT:    Logical bounds of the string
00433  * @param pRectInk      OUT:    Real pixel bounds of the string
00434  *
00435  * @return HxResult:            If result is not HX_OK, *pRectLogical and
00436  *                              *pRectInk are not defined.
00437  *
00438  **/
00439 HxResult HxFontGetStringExtents(HxFont_t* pFont, const char* pString,
00440                         HxRectangle_t* pRectLogical, HxRectangle_t* pRectInk);

00464  *                              to 0, if the width argument <= 0.
00465  *
00466  **/
